journey.name: paykit spark route
journey.description:
Proves that paying a Paykit contact whose only endpoint is on-chain, from a wallet whose spending balance is held on Spark, routes through a Spark withdrawal straight to the contact's address, without the user picking a route, and that the contact receives the exact amount on chain.
Preconditions: a dev debug build with E2E=true, E2E_BACKEND=local, E2E_HOMESERVER_PUBKY set to the local marketplace homeserver; bitkit-docker's default stack with the marketplace and payment-requests profiles; adb reverse for 6286, 6287, 6288, 15411, 15412, 60001, 23735, 23000 and 23010. The wallet has no channels and an empty savings balance, a Spark balance of at least 25 000 sats from Lightspark's regtest faucet sent to the deposit address on the Spark screen, a Pubky profile on the local homeserver, and the fixture-issuer's pubky saved as a contact. The contact is bitkit-docker's fixture-issuer, which publishes only a btc-regtest-p2wpkh endpoint; Spark pays it on Lightspark's regtest chain.

actions.action: Verify the savings balance (tag "ActivitySavings") shows 0 and the spending balance (tag "ActivitySpending") is above 25 000
Tap the fixture-issuer (tag "SendContact_" followed by its pubky)
Verify the amount screen (tag "send_amount_screen") offers SPENDING as the source
Verify the Confirm screen (tag "SendConfirm") is visible, then tap Show Details (tag "SendConfirmToggleDetails")
Verify FROM is SPENDING, TO is the contact, and ROUTE (tag "ReviewSwapRoute") reads "Spark"
Verify the Bitcoin Sent screen (tag "SendSuccess") shows 20 000
Verify Lightspark's regtest mempool shows the withdrawal transaction paying exactly 20 000 sats to the fixture-issuer's address
